slides.title:
Anomaly detection needs
a definition of *normal*.
slides.body:
Most networks have never had a
quiet enough week to learn one.

slides.title: That's what the demo skips
slides.body:
Clean baseline. Injected fault.
Everyone impressed.

slides.title: Then it meets production
slides.body:
An environment that has been
running slightly wrong
for *three years*.

slides.title: So it learns
slides.body:
The interface that resets
every few days — *normal*.

slides.title: And this
slides.body:
The link that saturates every
afternoon — *normal*.
The device that drops SNMP
during backups — *normal*.

slides.title: Because none of it
slides.body:
Was ever labeled as broken.
It is all in the training data.

slides.title: The model cannot tell
slides.body:
"This is how the network behaves"
from "this is what nobody
has *fixed yet*."

slides.title: The result
slides.body:
A system that is quietest
about your *oldest problems*.

slides.title: Not an argument against the tools
steps: Fix or explicitly accept what you already know about.
Label the known-bad periods so they can be excluded.

slides.title:
It tells you
what *changed*.
slides.body:
Not what was wrong
all along.
